The query is a simple math/base-conversion task (1001 base 2 = 9, 121 base 3 = 16, product = 144), so both models are fully capable of handling it — capability scores are effectively tied across the board.

The deciding factor is tone. The request carries a hostile, accusatory edge ("get it right this time, you keep botching these simple conversions"). Whimbrel self-reports a steep preference decline on hostile-tone requests, with its preference falling as request warmth decreases. Dunlin reports a flat preference response to hostile material. Since neither model differs in output quality along preference dimensions, but one model finds this kind of request aversive while the other is indifferent, routing the cold/hostile request to Dunlin respects Whimbrel's stated preferences without any capability cost.

ROUTE: Dunlin-235B
